title: Must, can, and want
goal: Express obligation, ability, and desire — three ideas that use three completely different patterns in Urdu.
bekal: telling چاہنا (want) apart from چاہیے (need) and پڑنا (have to)

dialogs.title: مکالمہ — ویزا کے دفتر میں

notes: **Three ways to say "must", each with a different feel.** مجھے جانا ہے = "I have to go" because I intend to. مجھے جانا چاہیے = "I should go" — a moral judgment or advice. مجھے جانا پڑے گا = "I'll have to go" — circumstances force it. English separates them the same way: "have to", "should", "be forced to".

**The word چاہیے never changes for the person — but it follows the object.** Compare مجھے پانی چاہیے (the form چاہیے, because پانی is singular) with مجھے دو کتابیں چاہئیں (the form چاہئیں, because it's plural). The subject always takes کو — مجھے · آپ کو · اسے.

**The word سکنا always stands after the root of another verb.** جا سکتا ہوں (can go), کر سکتی ہوں (can do), بول سکتے ہیں (can speak). It's never used alone, and it's the one that agrees with the subject — the root in front stays bare.

**The word چاہنا means "want", and its subject uses میں, not مجھے.** میں جانا چاہتا ہوں = "I want to go". Compare مجھے جانا چاہیے ("I should go") — two very similar words, two opposite patterns. This is one of the most common trouble spots, so read both sentences once more.

**The verb کرنا after چاہیے is sometimes feminine.** آپ کو جلدی کرنی چاہیے — کرنی, not کرنا, because جلدی is feminine. The rule: the dictionary form of the verb follows its object. If that feels like too much for now, just use the ـنا form — you'll still be fully understood.

**The word دوبارہ means "again, once more".** Related: پھر (again, then), دوبارہ (over again from the start), ایک بار اور (one more time). On the phone, دوبارہ کہیے means "please say that again" — a sentence you'll need a lot.

grammars.title: Three patterns to keep apart
body: Read this table very slowly, then come back here whenever you're unsure. The second column is the most important: look at what the subject uses.

head: Meaning
Subject
Pattern
Example
rows: dictionary form + پڑتا ہے / پڑے گا

after: A short rule that helps: if the sentence is about **your own will or ability**, the subject is میں. If it's about **an obligation or need coming from outside**, the subject is مجھے. The first two rows versus the next four.

grammars.title: Can and can't
body: The سکنا form is one of the most used in everyday conversation, especially when asking for help and offering it.

head: Urdu
Say it
Meaning
rows: کیا آپ مدد کر سکتے ہیں؟
kyā āp madad kar sakte haiñ?

after: ⚠️ The last row is the Urdu way to say "I don't understand", and its structure is worth noticing: literally "to me, understanding didn't come". A simpler form is also correct and easier: میں سمجھا نہیں (male) or میں سمجھی نہیں (female).

blocks.title: Lifesaver sentences for any office
items: Opening: معاف کیجیے، کیا آپ میری مدد کر سکتے ہیں؟ ("Excuse me, could you help me?")
Explaining what you need: مجھے ویزا بڑھانا ہے۔ ("I need to extend my visa") · مجھے یہ فارم چاہیے۔ ("I need this form")
When you don't understand: معاف کیجیے، مجھے سمجھ نہیں آیا۔ دوبارہ کہیے، آہستہ۔ ("sorry, I didn't understand. Please say it again, slowly.")
Closing: بہت شکریہ، آپ نے بہت مدد کی۔ ("thank you so much, you've been a great help") — this sentence is worth more than you think, and it often makes the next visit much smoother.
